issues.legal_issue: Compensation for surrender or sterilisation of rights forming part of a business’s profit-making apparatus is a capital receipt rather than a taxable trading receipt.
material_facts: The company held long-term forest leases under which it could fell trees, convert them into logs, and remove them, and it had made substantial investments in infrastructure and operations connected with those leases.
The leases and related assets were taken over following nationalisation of forest operations, and the company surrendered its residuary rights in return for logs or other compensation.
The court found that the leases affected the structure of the company’s operations and were capital assets, not merely stock-in-trade.
issues.conclusion: The compensation for cancellation or sterilisation of the forest-lease rights was a capital receipt and was not liable to tax. The sum awarded for rights under the leases in the area taken over earlier was likewise not taxable.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a receipt is capital or revenue depends on the facts and the nature of the asset and the business in which it was employed. Compensation for immobilisation, sterilisation, destruction, or loss of a capital asset is a capital receipt; compensation for taking over stock-in-trade is ordinarily a trading receipt. An agreement affecting the structure of the profit-making apparatus, rather than an ordinary commercial contract incidental to trade, may be a capital asset. The court relied on sections 10(2)(vii) and 41(2) as identified in the judgment, and referred to Glenboig Union Fireclay Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Inland Revenue; Senairam Doongarmall v. Commissioner of Income-tax; Commissioner of Income-tax, U.P. v. Gangadhar Baijnath; Commissioner of Income-tax, Poona v. Manna Ramji and Co.; Van Den Berghs Ltd. v. Clark; British Insulated & Helsby Cables Ltd. v. Atherton; Hood Barrs v. Commissioners of Inland Revenue (No. 2); and Commissioner of Income-tax, Hyderabad-Deccan v. Vazir Sultan & Sons.

rule.if: tax_appeal and long_term_operating_rights and rights_structured_business_operations and compensation_for_surrender_of_rights and not rights_merely_stock_in_trade

predicates.tax_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning the tax treatment of receipts from a business arrangement.
predicates.long_term_operating_rights: The business held continuing rights to conduct operations over an area, rather than rights confined to acquiring or selling ordinary trading stock.
predicates.rights_structured_business_operations: The rights regulated or materially formed the structure of the business’s profit-making operations.
predicates.compensation_for_surrender_of_rights: The business received compensation in return for giving up or losing those operating rights.
predicates.rights_merely_stock_in_trade: The rights were merely rights to obtain or dispose of stock-in-trade in the ordinary course of business.

issues.definition: When a tax appeal concerns compensation for surrendering operating rights that structured the business, and those rights were not merely stock-in-trade, the compensation is treated as capital and not taxable.

issues.legal_issue: A balancing charge cannot be imposed where depreciable assets were not sold for an agreed price and the arrangement instead provided compensation in kind.
material_facts: Under an agreement arising from nationalisation, the company handed over depreciable assets and received logs in return.
The company paid no money as a price for the assets delivered to it by the government.
The court found that the agreement did not involve a sale between the company and the government.
issues.conclusion: The logs’ sale proceeds could not be brought to tax as a balancing charge under the second proviso to section 10(2)(vii) of the Income-tax Act, 1922.
issues.legal_principle: For a balancing charge under the second proviso to section 10(2)(vii) of the Income-tax Act, 1922, the depreciable assets must have been sold at a price agreed between the parties. A transfer in exchange, involving reciprocal transfers of property, is not a sale for that purpose. The court referred to Commissioner of Income-tax v. Motors & General Stores (P) Ltd.

rule.if: tax_appeal and depreciable_assets_transferred and compensation_received_in_kind and no_agreed_sale_price

predicates.tax_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning the tax treatment of a business transaction.
predicates.depreciable_assets_transferred: The taxpayer transferred assets on which depreciation had been allowed or claimed.
predicates.compensation_received_in_kind: The taxpayer received property or goods rather than money as compensation for the transferred assets.
predicates.no_agreed_sale_price: The parties did not agree on a money price for a sale of the transferred assets.

issues.definition: If a tax appeal concerns transferred depreciable assets for which compensation was received in kind without an agreed sale price, a balancing charge is not imposed.

issues.legal_issue: Proceeds from logs received as compensation for business assets and residuary rights are not revenue receipts merely because the logs are later sold.
material_facts: The company received logs under an agreement made in consequence of nationalisation and in return for surrendering residuary rights and handing over depreciable assets, stores, and livestock.
The company kept the logs in a separate asset-realisation reserve account and did not mix them with its ordinary stock-in-trade.
The logs were sold over several years, and the dispute concerned the taxability of excess realisations over the cost attributed to obtaining delivery.
issues.conclusion: The proceeds, including the excess realisations, were not received on revenue account and were not liable to tax as trading receipts.
issues.legal_principle: The character of a receipt depends on the nature of the transaction and the role of the asset in the taxpayer’s business. What is a capital asset in one person’s hands may be a trading asset in another’s; the nature of the trade and the way the asset was employed are material. Compensation for loss or sterilisation of a capital asset is capital, while a sum representing trading profit in a new form is income. The court applied the capital-versus-revenue principles discussed in Senairam Doongarmall v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Commissioner of Income-tax, U.P. v. Gangadhar Baijnath, and Commissioner of Income-tax, Hyderabad-Deccan v. Vazir Sultan & Sons.

rule.if: tax_appeal and logs_received_as_compensation and logs_given_for_business_assets_or_rights and logs_kept_separate_from_trading_stock

predicates.tax_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning the tax treatment of receipts from a business transaction.
predicates.logs_received_as_compensation: The taxpayer received logs as compensation under an arrangement ending or altering its business operations.
predicates.logs_given_for_business_assets_or_rights: The logs were provided in return for business assets or rights surrendered to another party.
predicates.logs_kept_separate_from_trading_stock: The taxpayer kept the received logs apart from its ordinary stock-in-trade.

issues.definition: When a taxpayer receives logs for surrendered business assets or rights and keeps them separate from ordinary trading stock, their later sale proceeds are not treated as revenue receipts.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation received for stores acquired by the government is taxable where the taxability of that compensation was upheld on the facts before the court.
material_facts: The company received compensation of Rs. 9,493 for stores acquired by the government.
The High Court had answered in the affirmative the question whether that compensation was liable to tax.
No argument on behalf of the company had been advanced on that question before the High Court, and the Supreme Court upheld the High Court’s answer.
issues.conclusion: The compensation for the stores was held liable to tax.
issues.legal_principle: The court upheld the High Court’s answer in light of the principles involved and the nature of the transactions. The judgment does not state a further specific test for this compensation.

predicates.tax_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning the tax treatment of compensation received by a business.
predicates.compensation_received_for_stores_acquire: The taxpayer received compensation for stores acquired by another party.
predicates.taxability_of_store_compensation_upheld: The court upheld a determination that the compensation for the stores was liable to tax.

issues.definition: When a tax appeal concerns compensation for acquired stores and the court upholds its taxability, the compensation is taxable.
